houdini_version_notes: PDG/TOPs is Python-first; VEX appears only in the SOP cook a work item triggers. A Wedge TOP writes the wedge value onto geometry as a detail attribute.
title: Drive a Wedge from a PDG Detail Attribute
prompt: Use a per-work-item wedge value inside a SOP cooked by PDG
explanation: PDG itself is orchestrated in Python, so the only real VEX surface is the SOP cook a work item drives. Reading the wedged value from a detail attribute lets one network emit many deterministic variants, one per work item.

houdini_version_notes: PDG passes the work item index in as a detail attribute or parameter; VEX just records it.
alternative_prompts: tag geometry with work item index
title: Stamp the Work-Item Index onto Geometry
prompt: Record which PDG work item produced a piece of geometry
explanation: Stamping the work item index onto the geometry lets a downstream merge or ROP identify and order outputs that came back from many parallel TOP cooks. It underlines that VEX's role in TOPs is small and bookkeeping-oriented -- the orchestration lives in Python.
